svg.text: Quran memorization tracking on a student + teacher model. One NestJS API serves one Flutter app and one Next.js dashboard.
thin shell: routing, DI wiring, composition only
env config · Result<T, Failure> · Quran constants
packages/contracts is the source of truth. Every DTO is a zod schema with inferred TypeScript
types; the API validates with them and the web app imports the same schemas for form
OpenAPI is emitted from the controllers and then fanned out to both languages. pnpm gen:dart
writes the Dart client; pnpm gen:api-types writes the paths and components types that
openapi-fetch consumes in the web SDK.
Generated types give compile-time safety, the zod schemas stay the runtime guard, and
api-sdk/src/contract-check.ts asserts the two still agree so drift fails tsc.
Apps never import one another. Everything that crosses a boundary is HTTP under /api/v1.
Generated code is rewritten wholesale, so no hand edit survives. CI regenerates and fails on any diff.
The CI job drift re-runs all three generators and fails on any committed difference.
apps/* never import each other. Cross-app traffic is the API.
Every package exposes one public entry. Deep imports are forbidden.
ESLint boundaries and the shared tsconfig presets turn a violation into a build error.
turbo (TypeScript) and melos (Dart) order the task graph across both toolchains.
POST /auth/login returns an access + refresh JWT pair.
JwtStrategy guards routes; @Roles + RolesGuard enforce the role.
Optimistic write; a client UUID travels as the Idempotency-Key.
A 4xx domain rejection is surfaced to the student and never queued.
A 5xx or network failure goes to the drift outbox and retries with the same key.
A teacher sees what their students logged from the app.
Deliberately absent: a full sync engine and conflict resolution. Concurrent edits resolve
Postgres 16 service · turbo run lint typecheck test build
melos bootstrap · melos run analyze · melos run test
regenerate every client, then git diff --exit-code
